title: Tall Timber
objective: After this level you can explain how new wood products allow wooden high-rises.
summary: Cross-laminated timber glues boards in crossing layers, making stiff panels. Thick timber chars slowly, insulating its core. Ascent in Milwaukee (CTBUH, 2022) mixes mass timber with concrete.

cards.headline: In 2022, a 25-story tower was named the world's tallest timber building.
cards.body: The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) certified Ascent, in Milwaukee, at 86.6 meters. Remember Level 6: after the fire of 1666, London rebuilt in brick for protection from fire. So how does a wooden high-rise make sense?

cards.headline: Boards, crossed and glued
cards.body: The key product is cross-laminated timber, or CLT: layers of lumber boards stacked crosswise, typically at right angles, and glued together, at least three layers thick. It was introduced in the early 1990s in Austria and Germany. Crossing the layers is the whole point. A crossed panel is stable, strong and stiff in both directions, so it can make wide floor slabs and whole walls. Here's an analogy: a woven mat holds together far better than a pile of loose straws.

cards.headline: Why a thick timber survives a fire
cards.body: Wood burns, but thick wood burns slowly and predictably. Fire turns its surface to char, and that char insulates the wood inside, slowing the damage. In a standard fire test, wood chars at an average of about 0.6 mm per minute. A timber's strength depends on how much solid wood is left, so a thick one keeps much of its strength while its outside burns away. Here's an analogy: a big log on a campfire, black outside, solid inside.

cards.context: Ascent is a hybrid. Its base and its elevator and stair shafts are concrete; 19 of its 25 stories are mass timber, built from CLT and glulam. Before it rose, the USDA Forest Products Laboratory worked with its designers to test how a three-hour fire would affect its glulam columns. Level 6 said wood is strong for its weight; tall timber puts that strength to work, and plans for the fire.

mascot.line: London swapped wood for brick. Milwaukee brought wood back, and tested it in fire first.

cards.headline: Tall timber: raised
learned: CLT: boards in crossing layers, glued; early 1990s
Crossed layers: stable and stiff both ways
Char insulates thick timber, so its core keeps its strength
Ascent (2022): timber on a concrete base and cores

questions.prompt: In 2022, what did CTBUH certify Milwaukee's Ascent to be?

options.label: The world's tallest building of any kind
options.rationale: Far taller towers hold that record; Ascent's record is for timber.

options.label: The first tall building on a steel skeleton
options.rationale: That was Chicago's Home Insurance Building, Level 8.

options.label: The first 3D-printed apartment tower
options.rationale: Ascent was built from CLT and glulam, not printed.

questions.explanation: CTBUH certified the 25-story, 86.6-meter Ascent as the world's tallest timber building in 2022.

questions.prompt: Why are the layers of a cross-laminated timber (CLT) panel laid crosswise?

options.label: To use up short, leftover boards
options.rationale: The crossing is about stability and stiffness.

options.label: To let air flow between the boards
options.rationale: The layers are glued tight together.

options.label: To make it stable and stiff in both directions
So that it burns faster and more evenly
options.rationale: Nobody wants a floor that burns faster.

questions.explanation: Cross-laminating gives CLT stability, strength and stiffness in both directions, good for wide slabs and walls.

questions.prompt: After 1666, London rebuilt in brick for protection from fire (Level 6). Why can a thick timber column still hold up in a fire?

options.label: Modern wood can no longer catch fire
options.rationale: It burns, just slowly and predictably.

options.label: It is soaked in water before use
options.rationale: Protection comes from charring, not soaking.

options.label: Its glue melts and seals any cracks
options.rationale: The char layer does the protecting.

options.label: Its char insulates the solid wood inside

questions.explanation: Fire chars the surface, and the char insulates the core, which keeps much of its strength.
